title: Colours and Where Things Are
overview: Say the colour of a thing. Say what a thing is like: big, new, empty. Say where it is: in, on, at, near, next to. Point and say here and there.
learningPath: Words: look at the picture first. Guess. Then listen.
Patterns: 4 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read the 3 texts. Draw one room.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about a room. A made-up room is OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 3.
In this unit, you say what a thing is like.
And you say where it is.
First, ten colours. Listen and repeat.
Red. Blue. Green. Yellow. Black.
White. Brown. Orange. Pink. Grey.
Look at your bag. What colour is it?
Say: My bag is black. Or: My bag is blue.
Now put the colour first.
The bag is red. It is a red bag.
The box is big. It is a big box.
Red, then bag. Big, then box.
Empty, orange and old start with e and o.
So say an: an empty box. An orange cup. An old bag.
Two bags? Red has no s. Two red bags.
Now it is and it has.
This room is big. It is new.
It has two windows. It has a green door.
Is: big, new, red. Has: a door, two windows.
Not: It have a door. Say: It has a door.
Now, where is it? Listen.
The key is in the bag. You cannot see it.
The book is on the shelf.
Mia is at the desk.
The chair is near the window.
The bin is next to the table.
Next to is two words. Say both.
Now here and there.
Here: near you. There: not near you.
Point at your phone. Say: My phone is here.
Point at a door. Say: The door is there.
Not: Is here. Say: It is here.
Last, a new word. Listen and think.
The mat is on the floor, next to the door.
It is brown. It is dirty.
What is a mat? A thing on the floor, near the door.
The words near a new word can help you.
Now go to Words. Look at each picture first. Goodbye!

outcomes.outcome: Name ten colours, and put a colour or a describing word before the thing: a red bag, an empty box.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 1 practice self-checked; Practice 1 and 6 against the key; Speaking 1 recording; Writing 1 checklist; Quiz items 1 to 4 and 11.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say a red bag and a big box.

outcomes.outcome: Say and write what a thing is like and what it has, with it is and it has.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 2 practice; Practice 2, eight items; Speaking 2 recording; Writing 2 against its checklist; Quiz items 5 and 6.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write: It is big. It has a door.

outcomes.outcome: Say where things and people are with in, on, at, near and next to.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 3 practice; Practice 3, eight items; Speaking 3 recording; Writing 3 and 4 checklists; Quiz items 7 and 8.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say: The pen is on the desk.

outcomes.outcome: Ask where a thing is, and answer with here or there while you point.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 4 practice; Practice 4; Speaking 4 and 6 recordings; Quiz items 9 and 10.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can ask: Where is it? I can say: It is here.

outcomes.outcome: Read a short text about a room, find the colours and the places, and draw what it says; guess a word from its picture before reading its meaning.
outcomes.evidence: Words page: guess each word from its picture first; Practice 5 drawing checked against the key; Reading 1 questions 1, 2 and 4; Reading 3 questions 8 to 10.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can read about a room and draw it.

outcomes.evidence: The new word mat in the lesson; Speaking 5 answers checked against the key; Reading 1 question 3; Quiz item 12.

words.meaning: A colour: the colour of a tomato.
practice: Two red cups are on the shelf.
words.tutor: Name three red things you can see, like a red book. Ask the tutor to check that red came before the thing each time.

words.meaning: A colour: the colour of the sky on a sunny day.
practice: I have got a blue watch.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two blue things and two red things. Ask it to say one back with the wrong colour, and catch the mistake.

words.meaning: A colour: the colour of grass and leaves.
words.tutor: Green has two e letters together. Spell green to the tutor and ask it to check them.

words.meaning: A colour: the colour of the sun.
practice: The yellow cup is on the table.
words.tutor: Yellow has two l letters. Spell it to the tutor, then say it in two parts: YEL-low.

words.meaning: A colour: the colour of the sky at night.
practice: Two black pens are in the box.
words.tutor: Say black, then bag, to the tutor. Ask it whether the bl at the start of black was clear.

words.meaning: A colour: the colour of milk.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for three white things in a room, like a white wall. Say each one back with white first.

words.meaning: A colour: the colour of wood and of coffee.
practice: I have got a brown hat.
words.tutor: Describe two brown things near you to the tutor, with no names. Ask it to guess the things from your words.

words.meaning: A colour: red and yellow together.
words.tutor: Say an orange before three things, like an orange bag. Ask the tutor to check you said an, not a.

words.meaning: A colour: red and white together.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor what red and white make together. Then ask it two more colour mixes, and answer them yourself.

words.meaning: A colour: black and white together.
words.tutor: This course writes grey with an e. Type grey for the tutor and ask it to check the letters.

words.meaning: Not small. A bus is big.
words.tutor: Name two big things and two small things near you. Ask the tutor to check big came before the thing: a big desk.

words.meaning: Big from end to end, like a bus or a big table.
practice: The room has a long wall.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to name five things in a room. Say long or short for each one, and see if it agrees.

words.meaning: Not long. Small from end to end.
practice: The pen is long. The pencil is short.
words.tutor: Describe a long thing and a short thing to the tutor, like a long table and a short pencil. Ask it which is which.

words.meaning: Not old. It is from the shop today.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one new thing and one old thing you have got. Use It is new. It is old.

words.meaning: With nothing bad on it. Ready to use: a clean cup.
words.tutor: Say three lines like The cup is clean. Then say each one again as a clean cup. Ask the tutor to check the order.

words.meaning: Not clean. Wash it!
practice: The desk is not dirty. It is clean.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to say clean or dirty five times, in any order. Write C or D each time, then check with it.

words.meaning: With a lot in it. No more can go in.
practice: The shelf is full of books.
words.tutor: Name three things near you that can be full, like a bag or a bottle. Tell the tutor if each one is full or empty now.

words.meaning: With nothing in it: an empty box.
practice: My bag is not empty. It has a key in it.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor: Is my cup full or empty? Let it guess. Then say the answer in one line: It is an empty cup.

words.meaning: A place in a building, with walls and a door.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about one room, made up if you like: big or small, and the colour of the walls.

words.meaning: It has four legs. You can put cups and books on it.
words.example: The cups are on the table.
practice: My book is on the table.
words.tutor: Describe a table to the tutor in three lines: its colour, long or short, and one thing on it.

words.meaning: You can sit on it. It has four legs.
words.example: The chair is next to the desk.
practice: My bag is on the chair.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor where a chair is in a room, like The chair is next to the desk. Ask it to check you said to after next.

words.meaning: You go in and out of a room here.
practice: Is the door near the window?
My bag is next to the door.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor Where is the door? about a made-up room, and let it answer. Then answer its question: Where is the window?

words.meaning: Glass in a wall. You can look out of it.
practice: The desk is next to the window.
words.tutor: Window ends in ow, like yellow. Say window and yellow to the tutor and ask it to check the end sound.

words.meaning: You can walk on it. Tables and chairs are on it.
words.example: My bag is on the floor.
practice: The box is on the floor, near the door.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor: Is the bag on the floor or on the chair? Let it answer, then ask it two more like it.

words.meaning: A side of a room. You can put a picture on it.
practice: A photo is on the wall.
Is the desk next to the wall?
words.tutor: Tell the tutor the colour of each wall in a made-up room. Use the and is every time: The wall is blue.

words.meaning: A long thing on a wall. You can put books on it.
words.example: My books are on the shelf.
practice: Is the cup on the shelf?
The shelf is next to the window.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to name five things. Say yes if it can go on a shelf, like a book, and no if it cannot, like a door.

words.meaning: A table for work. You can read and write at it.
words.example: The desk is near the window.
practice: My pen is on the desk.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor three things on a desk, at school or at work. Say each one with on the desk: A pen is on the desk.

grammar.title: A red bag, a big box
grammar.explanation:
Red, big and new say what a thing is like.
Put the word first. Then the thing.
A red bag. A big box.
grammar.rule:
a colour, then the thing:
a red bag
a blue pen
a green door

big, long or new, then the thing:
a big box
a long table
a new desk

After is, the word is last:
The bag is red.
The box is big.

Empty, orange and old start with e and o. Use an:
an empty box
an orange cup
an old bag

Two things: the s is on the thing.
two red bags
grammar.workedExample:
The chair is grey. It is a ___ ___.
1. Grey is a colour.
2. The colour goes first.
3. Then the thing: chair.
4. Write: It is a grey chair.
5. Check: colour, then thing. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to put the colour last.
No: a bag red.
Yes: a red bag.
No: a box big.
Yes: a big box.
grammar.tip: Colour first, then the thing: a red bag.
grammar.practice:
Write it the short way.
1. The bag is red. It is a ___ ___.
2. The box is big. It is a ___ ___.
3. The door is green. It is a ___ ___.
4. The cup is empty. It is an ___ ___.
5. The desk is new. It is a ___ ___.
6. The pens are blue. They are ___ ___.
7. The bottle is orange. It is an ___ ___.
grammar.answers:
1. red bag  2. big box  3. green door  4. empty cup  5. new desk  6. blue pens  7. orange bottle
Wrong on 6? Blue has no s. The s is on pens.
Numbers 4 and 7 have an: empty and orange start with e and o.

grammar.title: It is big. It has a door.
grammar.explanation:
It is: say what a thing is like.
It has: say what a thing has.
Say it has. Not: it have.
grammar.rule:
It is: big, red, new
It is big.
It is red.
It is a new room.

It has: a thing
It has a door.
It has two windows.
It has four legs.

The room and the table: is and has.
The room is clean.
The table has four legs.
grammar.workedExample:
Look: a chair. It is brown. Four legs.
Say it in two lines.
1. Brown is a colour: It is brown.
2. Legs are things: It has four legs.
3. Write: It is brown. It has four legs.
4. Check: is with brown, has with legs. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to say have for it.
No: It have a window.
Yes: It has a window.
No: The room have two doors.
Yes: The room has two doors.
grammar.tip: Is: big, red, new. Has: a door, two windows.
grammar.practice:
Write is or has.
1. The room ___ big.
2. It ___ two windows.
3. The chair ___ brown.
4. It ___ four legs.
5. The desk ___ new.
6. It ___ a long shelf.
7. The cup ___ empty.
8. The room ___ a green door.
grammar.answers:
1. is  2. has  3. is  4. has  5. is  6. has  7. is  8. has
Big, brown, new, empty: is.
Windows, legs, a shelf, a door: has.
Wrong on 6? A shelf is a thing, so has.

grammar.title: In, on, at, near, next to
grammar.explanation:
These small words say where a thing is.
Ask: Where is the key?
Say: It is in the bag.
grammar.rule:
in: The key is in the bag.
on: The book is on the shelf.
at: Mia is at the desk.
near: The chair is near the window.
next to: The bin is next to the table.

In the bag: you cannot see it.
On the bag: you can see it.
At: a person at a place: at the door, at the desk.
Next to: very near. Two words.
grammar.workedExample:
The key ___ the bag.
1. Look at the bag. Can you see the key? No.
2. You cannot see it: in.
3. Write: The key is in the bag.
4. Check: is, then in. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to leave out to.
No: The desk is next the door.
Yes: The desk is next to the door.
Next to is two words.
grammar.tip: In the bag. On the desk. Next to: two words.
grammar.practice:
Write in, on, at, near or next to.
1. The key is ___ the bag. You cannot see it.
2. The book is ___ the table. You can see it.
3. The desk is next ___ the window.
4. Ben is ___ the door. Hello, Ben!
5. The photo is ___ the wall.
6. The pens are ___ the box. You cannot see them.
7. The chair is ___ the window.
grammar.answers:
1. in  2. on  3. to  4. at  5. on  6. in  7. near or next to: both are right
Wrong on 3? Next to is two words. Write the to.
Number 4: near is right too. At says Ben is at the door.

grammar.title: Here and there
grammar.explanation:
Here: near you.
There: not near you.
Point when you say there.
grammar.rule:
here: near you
My phone is here.
Your key is here, in my bag.
Here it is!

there: not near you
The door is there.
Your cup is there, on the table.
Where is the bin? It is there, next to the desk.

Look: t and here make there.
grammar.workedExample:
Your pen is next to you. Where is it?
1. Next to you is near you.
2. Near you: here.
3. Say: My pen is here.
4. Check: here, not there. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to leave out it.
No: Where is my phone? Is here.
Yes: It is here.
English needs it: It is there.
grammar.tip: The word there has here in it. Both are places.
grammar.practice:
Write here or there.
1. Your pen is near you. My pen is ___.
2. The door is not near you. The door is ___.
3. Your key is in your bag, near you. My key is ___.
4. The window is not near you. Point. It is ___.
5. Your book is next to you. It is ___.
6. The bin is not near you. It is ___, next to the door.
grammar.answers:
1. here  2. there  3. here  4. there  5. here  6. there
Near you or next to you: here.
Not near you: there. Point when you say it.

readings.title: My Room
readings.setting: A room at home, at school or at work.
readings.passage:
This is my room.
It has one big window and a white door.
The walls are blue. The floor is grey.
My desk is next to the window.
My books are on the shelf.
A brown mat is on the floor, near the door.
My bag is here, on the chair.
My phone? It is there, on the desk.

readings.title: Full and Empty, Clean and Dirty
readings.genre: A short guide to words in twos
readings.setting: Things you can see every day.
readings.passage:
Two cups. Cup 1 is full. Cup 2 is empty.
Two pencils. Pencil 1 is long. Pencil 2 is short.
Two floors. Floor 1 is clean. Floor 2 is dirty.
Two watches. Watch 1 is new. Watch 2 is old.
Full and empty. Long and short.
Clean and dirty. New and old.

readings.title: A Sign in Room 3
readings.setting: A sign on the wall of a room at a library.
readings.passage:
ROOM 3 — PLEASE READ

Bags: on the shelf, next to the door.
Phones: in your bag.
Cups: on the long table, not on the desks.
Empty bottles: in the bin, near the window.

A clean room, please. Thanks!

comprehension.why: Line 4: My desk is next to the window.

comprehension.q: A brown mat is on the floor. What is a mat? Look at the words near it.
comprehension.a: A thing on the floor, near the door.
comprehension.why: Line 6: on the floor, near the door. So a mat is a thing on the floor.

comprehension.q: My bag is here, on the chair. Where is the person?
comprehension.why: Line 7: Here is near you. The bag is here, on the chair. So the chair is near the person.

comprehension.q: Pencil 1 is long. What is pencil 2?
comprehension.why: Line 2: Pencil 2 is short. Short is not long.
Line 4: Watch 1 is new. Watch 2 is old. New is not old.

The sign says:
Empty bottles: in the bin, near the window.

comprehension.q: You have got a bag. Where can it go?
comprehension.a: On the shelf, next to the door.
comprehension.why:
The sign says:
Bags: on the shelf, next to the door.

comprehension.q: You have got a full cup. Can it go on your desk?
comprehension.a: No. It can go on the long table.
comprehension.why:
The sign says:
Cups: on the long table, not on the desks.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — A red bag: colour first
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
a red bag
a blue cup
a green door
a yellow pencil
a black phone
a white wall
a brown desk
a grey chair
a pink card
an orange bottle
Tap the mic. Say the 10 lines.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: the colour first in all 10?
An before orange?
speaking.tutor: Say the ten lines to the tutor. Ask it to tell you any line where the colour came after the thing.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — It is, it has: one thing
speaking.instructions:
Look at a thing near you.
A bag, a phone or a cup.
Say 4 lines about it.
It is my ___.
It is ___.
It is a ___ ___.
It has ___.
Listen to one.
It is my bag.
It is black.
It is a big bag.
It has a key in it.
Tap the mic. Say your 4 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: is in lines 1 to 3? Has in line 4?
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Look at a thing near you.
A bag, a phone or a cup.
Say 4 lines about it.
It is my …
It is …
It is a … …
It has …
Listen to one.
It is my bag.
It is black.
It is a big bag.
It has a key in it.
Tap the mic. Say your 4 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: is in lines 1 to 3? Has in line 4?
speaking.tutor: Say your four lines to the tutor. Ask it to ask you one more question about the thing, and answer with it is or it has.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Where is it?
speaking.instructions:
Read about the room.
The key is in the bag.
The book is on the shelf.
The chair is near the window.
The bin is next to the desk.
Hana is at the door.
Now listen to each question. Say the answer.
Where is the key?
Where is the book?
Where is the chair?
Where is the bin?
Where is Hana?
Tap the mic. Say the 5 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check: It is or She is at the start?
Then in, on, near, next to or at?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to ask you Where is …? about five things in a made-up room. Answer each with a whole line, not one word.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Here and there: point and say
speaking.instructions:
Point at a thing near you. Say: My ___ is here.
Point at a thing not near you. Say: The ___ is there.
Listen to two.
My phone is here.
The door is there.
Now read A. Say B.
1. A: Where is my key? B: It is here, in my bag.
2. A: Where is the bin? B: It is there, near the door.
3. A: Where is your pen? B: It is here.
4. A: Where is the window? B: It is there.
Tap the mic. Say the 4 B lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: It is in all 4 lines?
Here for near you? There for not near?
A friend can say A. No one with you? Say A and B.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Point at a thing near you. Say: My … is here.
Point at a thing not near you. Say: The … is there.
Listen to two.
My phone is here.
The door is there.
Now read A. Say B.
1. A: Where is my key? B: It is here, in my bag.
2. A: Where is the bin? B: It is there, near the door.
3. A: Where is your pen? B: It is here.
4. A: Where is the window? B: It is there.
Tap the mic. Say the 4 B lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: It is in all 4 lines?
Here for near you? There for not near?
A friend can say A. No one with you? Say A and B.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor Where is my phone? and Where is the door? in a made-up room. Then it asks you. Answer with here or there.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — What is it? Listen and guess
speaking.instructions:
Listen to each one. Say what it is.
1. It is in a room. It is in a wall. You can look out of it.
2. It is yellow. It is hot. It is big. It is not in a room.
3. It has four legs. You can sit on it.
4. A new word: mug. The mug is on the table. It is big and white. It is full. It is hot. It is next to the cups. What is a mug?
Tap the mic. Say the 4 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 1. a window  2. the sun  3. a chair  4. a big cup.
Wrong on 4? Listen again: full, hot, next to the cups.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to describe a thing in a room in three short lines, with no name. Guess the thing. Then describe one for the tutor to guess.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — My bag, at the library desk
speaking.instructions:
You are at the desk at a library. Your bag is not here.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello! Can I help?
You: Hello. My bag, please. It is not here.
Desk: What colour is it?
You: It is ___.
Desk: Is it big?
You: Yes, it is big. Or: No, it is small.
Desk: What is in it?
You: It has a ___ in it.
Desk: Look. A bag is there, on the shelf.
You: Yes! It is there. Thanks!
Desk: Here it is. Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up bag.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: a colour? Has in your line? There at the end?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
You are at the desk at a library. Your bag is not here.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello! Can I help?
You: Hello. My bag, please. It is not here.
Desk: What colour is it?
You: It is …
Desk: Is it big?
You: Yes, it is big. Or: No, it is small.
Desk: What is in it?
You: It has a … in it.
Desk: Look. A bag is there, on the shelf.
You: Yes! It is there. Thanks!
Desk: Here it is. Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up bag.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: a colour? Has in your line? There at the end?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be the person at the library desk. Describe a made-up bag: its colour, big or small, and one thing in it.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Colour first
writing.prompt:
Write 6 things you can see now.
Put the colour first.
writing.model:
a black phone
a white wall
a brown table
a blue pen
a grey bag
a green book
writing.criteria:
6 lines.
A colour in each line.
The colour before the thing.
A or an at the start of each line.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change only the colours.
Then change the things.
writing.extension: Write 2 more with two things: two red cups. The s goes on the thing.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A thing you have got
writing.prompt:
Write 4 lines about a thing you have got.
A bag, a phone or a watch.
Use it is and it has.
writing.model:
This is my bag.
It is grey.
It is big.
It has a key and a pen in it.
writing.criteria:
4 lines.
Is in lines 2 and 3.
Has in line 4.
A capital letter and a full stop (.) in each.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change grey to a new colour.
Change big to small or new.
Change the key and the pen.
writing.extension: Write 2 lines about a room: It is ___. It has ___.

writing.title: Writing 3 — My room
writing.prompt:
Write 5 lines about a room.
Say where 3 things are.
It can be a made-up room.
writing.model:
My room is small.
It has one window.
The desk is next to the window.
My books are on the shelf.
My bag is on the floor.
writing.criteria:
5 lines.
In, on, at, near or next to in 3 lines.
Next to with its to.
A capital letter and a full stop (.) in each.
writing.support:
Draw the room on paper first.
Copy lines 3 to 5 of the model.
Change the things to the things in your picture.
writing.extension: Add 2 lines with here and there: My phone is here. The door is there.

writing.title: Writing 4 — A sign for a room
writing.prompt:
Write a sign like Reading 3.
Say where 4 things go.
writing.model:
ROOM 5
Bags: on the chair, next to the door.
Cups: on the long table.
Books: on the shelf.
Empty bottles: in the bin, near the window.
A clean room, please. Thanks!
writing.criteria:
4 things, each with a place.
In, on, near or next to in each line.
A colon (:) after each thing.
Please and thanks at the end.
writing.support:
Copy the sign in Reading 3.
Change the room number.
Change 2 places.
writing.extension: Add a colour to 2 things: Grey bags: on the shelf.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Colour first: word order
activities.instructions:
Put the words in order.
1. cup / blue / a
2. black / a / phone
3. door / green / a
4. an / box / empty
5. a / chair / grey
6. bags / two / red
7. table / long / a
8. an / bottle / orange
activities.answers:
1. a blue cup  2. a black phone  3. a green door  4. an empty box  5. a grey chair  6. two red bags  7. a long table  8. an orange bottle
Check 6: the s is on bags, not on red.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write each one on paper. Say it out loud. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Is or has
activities.instructions:
Write is or has.
1. The window ___ clean.
2. The room ___ one door.
3. It ___ white.
4. The chair ___ four legs.
5. My bag ___ full.
6. It ___ a phone in it.
7. The shelf ___ long.
8. The room ___ a grey floor.
activities.answers:
1. is  2. has  3. is  4. has  5. is  6. has  7. is  8. has
Clean, white, full, long: is.
A door, legs, a phone, a floor: has.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write your answers on paper. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.title: Practice 3 — In, on, at, near, next to
activities.instructions:
Write in, on, at, near or next to.
1. The phone is ___ my bag. I cannot see it.
2. The cups are ___ the shelf.
3. Ben is ___ the door. Hello, Ben!
4. The desk is next ___ the window.
5. The photo is ___ the wall.
6. The pens are ___ the box. I cannot see them.
7. The bin is ___ to the chair.
8. The table is ___ the door.
activities.answers:
1. in  2. on  3. at  4. to  5. on  6. in  7. next  8. near or next to: both are right
Number 3: near is right too.
Numbers 4 and 7: next to is two words.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud. Write the word. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Here or there
activities.instructions:
Write here or there.
1. Your phone is next to you. My phone is ___.
2. The window is not near you. The window is ___.
3. Your bag is on your chair. My bag is ___.
4. The bin is not near you. Point. It is ___.
5. Where is my key? It is ___, in my bag.
6. Where is the door? It is ___. Point.
7. Fix the spelling: Your cup is their.
activities.answers:
1. here  2. there  3. here  4. there  5. here  6. there  7. Your cup is there.
Number 7: their is for people: their bag. There is a place.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Pattern 4 and do it again.
activities.solo: Point as you say each line. Write the word. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Read and draw
activities.instructions:
Use paper and a pencil.
Read each line. Draw it.
1. The room has one window.
2. A long table is next to the window.
3. Two chairs are near the table.
4. A red cup is on the table.
5. A shelf is on the wall.
6. Three books are on the shelf.
7. A black bag is on the floor.
Now look at your picture and check it.
activities.answers:
Check your picture.
1. One window, not two?
2. The table is long, and next to the window?
3. Two chairs, near the table?
4. The cup is on the table? Is it red?
5. The shelf is on the wall?
6. Three books on the shelf?
7. The bag is on the floor, not on a chair?
6 or 7 yes: good.
5 or less: read the lines again and fix your picture.
activities.solo: Draw on paper. Read each check line. Count the yes lines.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Two words that go together
activities.instructions:
Match 1 to 8 with a to h.
1. full
2. clean
3. long
4. new
5. big
6. black and white
7. red and white
8. red and yellow
a. short
b. old
c. empty
d. small
e. dirty
f. grey
g. orange
h. pink
activities.answers:
1c  2e  3a  4b  5d  6f  7h  8g
Numbers 7 and 8: red and white is pink. Red and yellow is orange.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Reading 2 and the colour words again.
activities.solo: Say each pair out loud. Write the letters. Check with the key.

quizzes.why: The colour goes first, then the thing: a red bag. A bag red has the colour last. Red has no s. A comes before red, not after it.
Empty starts with e, so an: an empty box. A is for big, red and new. Two needs boxes, with an s. Is does not go before a thing.
Red and white: pink. Grey is black and white. Orange is red and yellow. Brown is the colour of wood.
The sun is yellow. It is hot and big. But hot and big are not colours. Blue is the sky.
Legs are things the chair has: has. Is is for a colour: The chair is brown. Have is for I and you, not for it. Are is for two or more.
Clean says what the window is like: is. Has is for a thing: It has a door. Have is for I and you. One window: is, not are.

options: The desk is next the window.
The desk is next of the window.
The desk is to next the window.
The desk is next to the window.
quizzes.a: The desk is next to the window.
quizzes.why: Next to is two words, in that order. Next the has no to. We do not say next of. To next is the wrong order.

quizzes.q: You cannot see the key. It is ___ the bag.
quizzes.why: You cannot see it. So it is in the bag. On the bag, you can see it. At is for a person: at the door. Here does not go before the bag.

quizzes.q: Your pen is next to you. Where is it?
quizzes.why: Next to you: here. There is for a thing not near you. Is here has no it. It here has no is.

quizzes.q: The chair is not near you. Your bag is on it. Your bag is ___.
quizzes.why: Not near you: there. Their is for people: their bag. Here is near you. These is for two or more things.

quizzes.q: The bottle has nothing in it. It is ___.
quizzes.why: Nothing in it: empty. Full has a lot in it. Dirty is not clean. Long is for a table or a bus.

quizzes.q: A new word: rug. The rug is on the floor. It is long and red. What is a rug?
quizzes.why: The rug is on the floor. So it is a thing on the floor. Red is its colour, not the rug. A door is in a wall. A room has walls and a floor.

teacherNotes.note: Every card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a checklist the learner can see. If you are helping, point at the checklist rather than correcting mid-sentence, and let the learner find the slip first.

teacherNotes.type: The one error worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: The colour after the thing: a bag red, a box big. In many languages the describing word follows the noun, so this feels natural. Notice it every time, gently, and give the same fix each time: colour first, then the thing. A second slip to watch is a plural -s on the colour (two reds bags).

Unit 2 teaches a and the. This unit is the first where the word after a is a describing word, and empty, orange and old start with a vowel, so an is forced on the learner. Pattern 1 explains it only as far as those three words need. Do not widen it into a lesson on vowels.

teacherNotes.type: Near and next to; there as a place
teacherNotes.note: Next to is a kind of near, so where both are true the keys accept both; do not mark near wrong for two things side by side. There in this unit is only a place (It is there, next to the door). There is and there are come in Unit 8; do not introduce them here.

teacherNotes.type: Words used on purpose without teaching them
teacherNotes.note: Three words appear untaught: mat (the lesson and Reading 1), mug (Speaking 5) and rug (Quiz 12). They exist so the learner can practise working out a new word from the words around it. Do not pre-teach them or add them to a word list. The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner only; a made-up room and made-up things are always fine.

selfAssessment.statement: I can say a red bag and a big box.
I can write: It is big. It has a door.
I can say where it is: on the desk.
I can point and say here and there.
I can read about a room and draw it.
I can listen and guess a new word.

assignment.title: A room in colour
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Say 5 lines about a room: its colours, what it has, and where 3 things are. Point and say one line with here and one with there.
2. Write your 5 lines, like Writing 3.
It can be a made-up room.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written text
